outcome: Morbidities (bronchopulmonary dysplasia, severe intraventricular hemorrhage, periventricular leukomalacia, necrotizing enterocolitis, sepsis, severe retinopathy of prematurity)
cohort: 9552 very preterm infants (gestational age < 32 weeks) admitted to 57 tertiary neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) in China between January 1 and December 31, 2019
finding: While survival and survival without major morbidity of very preterm infants in Chinese NICUs have improved, they remain lower than in high-income countries, highlighting the need for comprehensive quality improvement efforts to optimize obstetrical and neonatal care practices.
mod_finding: 54.8% of the very preterm infants were born through cesarean delivery.
